solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One with home duties has hob unused — strange!

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the three words before it are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A homemaker is puzzled that the hob has never been used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the twelve letters of HAS HOB UNUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who stays home to run the household and its chores is described by this term.

clue.text: Asian native managed to get involved in nougat supply

indicators.note: to get involved in means the word for managed is placed inside the other letters
supply read as the adverb of supple, so the word nougat is bent into a new shape

parts.note: to manage something is to run it, so managed gives ran

explanation.surface: Someone contrived to get mixed up in the delivery of a sweet nougat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb from 'supple', so it rearranges the sweet's name to OGUTAN; 'to get involved in' sets the other piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape so named is native to the forests of Borneo and Sumatra in Asia.

clue.text: Genuine, as welcoming former queen

indicators.note: welcoming means one word takes the other in, holding it inside

parts.note: as in 'as you were out' means since
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: Someone is sincere because they are greeting a queen of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' sets the queen's cipher inside the other piece; ER is Elizabeth Regina, former since her death in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms describing something honest and without pretence.

clue.text: Husky — vulgar, change at top needed

indicators.note: change at top needed tells the solver to swap the opening letter of the word for vulgar for another

parts.note: vulgar language is coarse

explanation.surface: Someone with a rough voice is crude, and the leadership must change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change at top needed' replaces the first letter, C, of COARSE with H; the clue does not name the new letter, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is a rough, croaky one, the synonym used for a strained throat.

clue.text: Son left on board game

parts.note: port is the left-hand side on board a ship

explanation.surface: A son left the room to play a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a board game, but it belongs with 'left': PORT is the left side aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is a game or competitive pastime, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Excitement in sandbox regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word sandbox, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A child gets excited playing in the sandbox often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of sANDbOx.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bustle, a commotion of the sort that excitement brings.

clue.text: One first to find records I've out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters of records and I've are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is first to notice that the records they own are disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges RECORDS and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who finds something before anyone else is the one credited with its discovery.

clue.text: Watering hole, northern — large building

parts.note: a watering hole is a slang name for a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A northern pub is housed in a large building.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a large farm building for storing grain or keeping animals.

clue.text: In love, glamorous first couple's leaving

indicators.note: first couple's leaving means the opening pair of letters of glamorous go away

explanation.surface: A glamorous pair is in love, but they are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple's leaving' drops GL from the front of GLAMOROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means feeling or showing romantic desire, the state of being in love.

clue.text: I'm chattier about working with figures

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of I'm chattier are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being more talkative than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IM and CHATTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics dealing with calculation using numbers.

clue.text: Move back — way out after resistance

indicators.note: after puts the word for way out following the letter for resistance

parts.note: R is the symbol for resistance in physics
an egress is an exit, a way out

explanation.surface: Retreat, as there is an exit behind the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places EGRESS behind R.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to go back to an earlier or less developed state, a retreat.

clue.text: Not the whole body? Ultimately right, approximately

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word right is taken

parts.note: approximately means or so, as in 'ten minutes or so'

explanation.surface: A question of whether a figure is complete, answered with roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes T from the end of 'right'; OR SO means approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the body without the head and limbs, so only part of it.

clue.text: Hard-nosed, referring to celebrities in charge

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to, as in business letters
the A-list is the group of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A tough-minded report about famous people who run things.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-nosed person is practical and unsentimental, seeing things as they are.

clue.text: Tense aquatic mammal to move unsteadily on land

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the otter is a water-loving mammal

explanation.surface: An anxious otter wobbles about when it leaves the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like a description of the otter's mood, but it gives only T.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk with unsteady, faltering steps, as someone on shaky legs does.

clue.text: One making buzz about conflict? Watch out!

indicators.note: about means the word for buzzing insect goes around the word for conflict

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A warning cry about something that is noisily stirring up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the conflict inside the buzzing insect; the question mark flags the indirect description of that insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are warning cries telling someone to be careful of a danger.

clue.text: Model test, simple? Not half!

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: Not half! means dropping one half of the word simple, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A test paper is not merely easy, it is extremely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like the British exclamation meaning 'very much', but here it removes SIM, half of SIMPLE, leaving PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is an example to follow, a specimen that shows how something should be.

clue.text: Disregard turbulent reign — nothing to be included

indicators.note: to be included means the letter for nothing is placed inside
turbulent means the letters of reign are stirred up

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Overlook a stormy reign in which nothing is achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges REIGN to IGNRE, and 'to be included' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay no attention to it, the same as refusing to notice.

clue.text: This writer's eating cold meat

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: this writer refers to the setter, so this writer's means mine
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A writer is eating some cold meat for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' places C inside MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is meat finely chopped or ground, used for dishes like burgers.

clue.text: Message system, easy, modern, appropriate, is liked at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset means the opening letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: A messaging service is described as handy, up to date, suitable and popular from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' takes the first letters of 'easy, modern, appropriate, is, liked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is the electronic mail system for sending messages between computers.

clue.text: Building material in great rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes, so the letters of in great are shaken up

explanation.surface: A building stone is found among great rock formations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like the noun, but is the verb that rearranges IN GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous stone widely used in construction and paving.

clue.text: Storm also surrounding navy commercial

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for also wraps round the other letters

parts.note: too means also
RN is the Royal Navy
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: A gale also hits a naval advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the word for also around the navy and advert pieces; RN is Britain's Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating storm with a funnel-shaped cloud.

clue.text: Feature of more valuable gun

indicators.note: Feature of means the letters are found as part of the phrase more valuable

explanation.surface: An extra-precious firearm has a special attribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature of' finds the run in moRE Valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: To gun an engine is to rev it, making it run faster by opening the throttle.

clue.text: Have compassion for Greek character, extremely touchy

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of touchy are taken

explanation.surface: Feel sorry for a very sensitive Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes T and Y, the ends of 'touchy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to feel sorrow and sympathy for their suffering.

clue.text: Polite plea — help in time of conflict

parts.note: civil means polite or courteous
a defence is a plea made in court

explanation.surface: A courteous request for help during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plea' looks like a request, but in a law court a plea is the defence offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil defence is the organisation of civilians to protect people during war or attack.
